title: GeoPurify: A Data-Efficient Geometric Distillation Framework for Open-Vocabulary 3D Segmentation
claim: Features from one source are semantically rich but geometrically fragmented, while features from another are structurally coherent but semantically blind, revealing a gap to bridge.
layout: 3 panels left-to-right (a)-(c): original scene, 2D-distilled segmentation with class legend, 3D geometric segmentation with 'unknown' legend
description: Three side-by-side renderings of the same indoor room point cloud, viewed from above at an angle. Panel (a) shows the original RGB scan with furniture and textured surfaces. Panel (b), titled '2D Distilled Features (Geometric Inconsistency)', shows a noisy, fragmented semantic segmentation colored by class (wall, floor, chair, table, sofa, etc.) with a named class legend on the right. Panel (c), titled '3D Geometric Features (Structural Coherence)', shows clean, compact, well-bounded segments in many colors, but every legend entry reads 'unknown', meaning no semantics. Bold serif titles sit above each panel and labels (a), (b), (c) sit below. The eye goes first to the colorful segmentations in the middle and right, then to the contrast between the named legend and the 'unknown' legend.
caption: The Fundamental Disconnect: Semantic Richness vs. Geometric Coherence. Left: Original RGB 3D scene. Middle: Features distilled from 2D VLMs [ref] offer rich semantics but exhibit geometric inconsistency, leading to fragmented and noisy segmentations. Right: Features from 3D self-supervised model [ref] provide strong structural coherence with geometrically sound segments, yet inherently lack open-vocabulary semantic understanding. Our proposed method aims to bridge this critical gap by purifying the semantically rich 2D features with robust 3D geometric priors.
abstract: Recent attempts to transfer features from 2D Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to 3D semantic segmentation expose a persistent trade-off. Directly projecting 2D features into 3D yields noisy and fragmented predictions, whereas enforcing geometric coherence necessitates costly training pipelines and large-scale annotated 3D data. We argue that this limitation stems from the dominant segmentation-and-matching paradigm, which fails to reconcile 2D semantics with 3D geometric structure. The geometric cues are not eliminated during the 2D-to-3D transfer but remain latent within the noisy and view-aggregated features. To exploit this property, we propose GeoPurify that applies a small Student Affinity Network to purify 2D VLM-generated 3D point features using geometric priors distilled from a 3D self-supervised teacher model. During inference, we devise a Geometry-Guided Pooling module to further denoise the point cloud and ensure the semantic and structural consistency. Benefiting from latent geometric information and the learned affinity network, GeoPurify effectively mitigates the trade-off and achieves superior data efficiency. Extensive experiments on major 3D benchmarks demonstrate that GeoPurify achieves or surpasses state-of-the-art performance while utilizing only about 1.5% of the training data.
